title: Feature-Aware (Hyper)graph Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
claim: A baseline generates structurally broken, collapsed samples, while our method produces outputs that closely match the true training examples.
layout: 2x3 grid, columns left-to-right: training, baseline, ours; dashed rounded frames
description: A grid with two rows and three columns. Each cell is a dashed rounded box holding a red, semi-transparent hypergraph drawn over blue nodes. The column titles are 'Training Examples', 'Disjoint Generation Baseline' and 'FAHNES'. The top row shows an airplane. The bottom row shows a sofa or bench. The training column has clean shapes with recognizable structure. The baseline column is badly distorted. The airplane is collapsed and stretched, with long thin spikes. abstract: Graph generative models perform well on small-scale structured data but struggle to scale to large, complex structures. Hierarchical approaches improve scalability but often ignore node and edge features, which are critical in real-world applications. In this paper, we propose FAHNES (feature-aware (hyper)graph generation via next-scale prediction), a hierarchical framework that jointly generates topology and features for graphs and hypergraphs. FAHNES progressively constructs the final sample through localized expansion and refinement, guided by a novel node budget controlling granularity and ensuring cross-scale consistency. Experiments on synthetic, 3D mesh, and graph point cloud datasets demonstrate competitive or state-of-the-art performance while uniquely scaling to large-scale graphs and hypergraphs with features. Our code is open source.
